title: Ogwumgwu (board thumb piano)
summary: The ogwumgwu is a board lamellophone set into a half gourd, played by Idoma men for personal amusement. Iron keys fixed on a board are plucked with the fingers while the player grips the instrument through two crescent-shaped sound holes cut in the board.
howToPlay: Every key is lit in order of pitch; the tip of each key is where the thumb plucks.
Notes fall toward a tip; strike it as the note lands. The key flexes and glows.
Start with the first cycle, then the answering one.
rules: A stroke on the pulse is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: It is played for private enjoyment rather than at public events, a quiet instrument held close to the body.
credits: Tradition: the ogwumgwu; cycles written for this game
